claims.text: Fe deficiency: always look for the cause (ex, a bleed site), even when the anemia = mild
claims.quote: Iron therapy without pursuit of the cause is poor practice; a bleeding site should be sought even in cases of mild anemia.

claims.text: Oral Fe: a typical starting dose = 65 mg elemental Fe (ex, 325 mg ferrous sulfate) QOD, taken 30 minutes AC
claims.quote: Oral iron can be provided by various iron salts (eg, ferrous sulfate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous fumarate) or saccharated iron given 30 minutes before meals (food or antacids may reduce absorption). A typical initial dose is 65 mg of elemental iron (eg, as 325 mg of ferrous sulfate) given every other day (1).

claims.text: IV Fe: works faster than oral Fe
claims.quote: Parenteral iron causes a more rapid therapeutic response than oral iron does

claims.text: IV Fe = for: intol of oral Fe, oral Fe ⍉working, steady lrg blood loss (ex, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia), or a need for fast repletion (severe anemia, elective surg, third trimester)
claims.quote: Parenteral iron is reserved for Patients who do not tolerate oral iron Patients for whom oral iron is ineffective Patients who steadily lose large amounts of blood because of capillary or vascular disorders (eg, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia) Patients with a need for expedient iron repletion due to severe anemia, elective surgery, or third trimester of pregnancy

claims.text: Expected response: reticulocytes rise after about 1 wk; Hb starts rising after 1 to 2 wks, about 1 g/dL by 14 days
claims.quote: Reticulocytosis usually occurs after 1 week, and Hb begins to rise after 1 to 2 weeks with an ~ 1 g/dL increase at 14 days in responders (2).

claims.text: How long: cont oral Fe ≥ 6 months after Hb normalizes, to refill stores
claims.quote: Oral iron therapy should continue for ≥ 6 months after correction of hemoglobin levels to replenish tissue stores

claims.text: Poor response: think of continued bleed, infect or CA, too little Fe intake, or poor absorb of oral Fe
claims.quote: A subnormal response suggests continued hemorrhage, underlying infection or cancer, insufficient iron intake, or malabsorption of oral iron.

claims.text: B12 deficiency, ⍉severe and ⍉neuro signs: vit B12 1000 to 2000 mcg orally Q1x day
claims.quote: Vitamin B12 1000 to 2000 mcg orally can be given once a day to patients who do not have severe deficiency or neurologic symptoms or signs.

claims.text: B12 deficiency, severe: vit B12 1 mg IM 1 to 4 × a wk for several wks until the blood counts correct, then once a mo
claims.quote: For more severe deficiency, vitamin B12 1 mg IM is usually given 1 to 4 times a week for several weeks until hematologic abnormalities are corrected; then it is given once a month.

claims.text: Response to tx: blood counts USU correct w.in 6 wks (reticulocytes w.in 1 wk); neuro Sx take much longer and become permanent if they last months to years
claims.quote: Although hematologic abnormalities are usually corrected within 6 weeks (reticulocyte count should improve within 1 week), resolution of neurologic symptoms may take much longer. Neurologic symptoms that persist for months or years become irreversible.

claims.text: B12 = lifelong: unless the cause of the deficiency = corrected
claims.quote: Vitamin B12 treatment must be continued for life unless the pathophysiologic mechanism for the deficiency is corrected.

claims.text: Folate deficiency: folate 400 to 1000 mcg orally Q1x day
claims.quote: Folate 400 to 1000 mcg orally once a day replenishes tissues and is usually successful even if deficiency has resulted from malabsorption.

claims.text: In megaloblastic anemia, r/o B12 deficiency b4 giving folate: folate can fix the anemia of B12 deficiency but does ⍉reverse, and may worsen, its neuro deficits
claims.quote: In patients with megaloblastic anemia, vitamin B12 deficiency must be excluded before treating with folate. If vitamin B12 deficiency is present, folate supplementation can alleviate the anemia but does not reverse, and may even worsen, neurologic deficits.

claims.text: Neutropenia w fever or hypotension: assume serious infect and give empiric, ↑dose, broad-spectrum IV abx right away
claims.quote: Suspected infections are always treated immediately. If fever or hypotension is present, serious infection is assumed, and empiric, high-dose, broad-spectrum antibiotics are given IV.

claims.text: Neutropenia from a drug or toxin: stop every poss culprit
claims.quote: If acute neutropenia is suspected to be caused by a medication or a toxin, all potential etiologic agents are stopped.

claims.text: G-CSF: speeds neutrophil recovery and prevents infect w intensive chemo and after stem cell transplant
claims.quote: Myeloid growth factors (ie, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor [G-CSF]) are widely used to accelerate neutrophil recovery and prevent infection in patients receiving intensive cancer chemotherapy and after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

claims.text: ITP w ⍉Sx or bleed, ⍉other bleed risks and PLT > 30,000/mcL: USU ⍉tx, just monitoring
claims.quote: Patients who have no symptoms, a platelet count > 30,000/mcL (> 30 × 109/L), no other bleeding risks (eg, anticoagulants) and no bleeding usually do not require treatment and can be monitored.

claims.text: Adults w newly diagnosed ITP, bleed and PLT < 30,000/mcL: USU an oral glucocorticoid, ex, prednisone 1 mg/kg Q1x day, or dexamethasone 40 mg Q1x day for 4 days
claims.quote: Adults with newly diagnosed ITP with bleeding and a platelet count < 30,000/mcL (< 30 × 109/L) are usually given an oral glucocorticoid (eg, prednisone 1 mg/kg orally once a day). An alternative, probably equally effective, glucocorticoid regimen is dexamethasone 40 mg orally once a day for 4 days.

claims.text: ITP w severe bleed: IVIG, IV anti-D immune globulin, IV glucocorticoids and/or platelet transfusions
claims.quote: For severe bleeding, IVIG, IV anti-D immune globulin, IV glucocorticoids, and/or platelet transfusions

claims.text: Platelet transfusion in ITP: for life-threatening bleed, ⍉given prophylactically
claims.quote: Patients with ITP and life-threatening bleeding are also given platelet transfusions. Platelet transfusions are not used prophylactically.
claims.locator: Treatment of ITP, Life-threatening bleeding in ITP
